item.vignette: A 16-year-old boy has progressive distal leg weakness, pes cavus, reduced ankle reflexes, and decreased vibration sensation. His maternal uncle is similarly affected, and there is no male-to-male transmission. Genetic testing identifies a hemizygous loss-of-function variant in GJB1.
item.lead_in: Which normal Schwann-cell function is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: Compaction of peripheral myelin by increased PMP22 gene dosage
options.B: Gap-junction transfer of ions and small molecules through connexin 32
options.D: Axonal transport of vesicles by dynein
options.E: Lysosomal degradation of sulfatides by arylsulfatase A

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires recognizing that GJB1 encodes connexin 32 and applying gap-junction physiology to Schwann cells.
item.tested_construct: GJB1/connexin-32 gap-junction function in Schwann cells in CMT1X

explanation.key_explanation: GJB1 encodes connexin 32, a gap-junction protein expressed in peripheral myelin at noncompact regions of Schwann cells. Gap junctions permit transfer of ions and small molecules; GJB1 loss disrupts this pathway in CMT1X.

distractor_explanations.A: PMP22 duplication causes CMT1A, a different hereditary neuropathy.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Connexin 32 forms gap-junction channels that allow passage of ions and small molecules through Schwann-cell myelin compartments.
distractor_explanations.C: MFN2-mediated mitochondrial fusion is implicated in CMT2A, not GJB1 disease.
distractor_explanations.D: Dynein-dependent retrograde axonal transport is not the primary GJB1 function.
distractor_explanations.E: Aryl­sulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy rather than CMT1X.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect GJB1 loss in CMT1X with impaired connexin-32 gap-junction communication in Schwann cells.

evidence_map.claim: GJB1 encodes connexin 32 in peripheral myelin; connexin gap junctions transfer ions and small molecules.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains the molecular defect in an X-linked hereditary neuropathy.
